official_primary_sources.finding: dxStepBody advances COM linearly, applies finite or normal Euler quaternion rotation, normalizes it, then damps stored velocities. Normal rotation is a special case that must be verified, not assumed from ODE name.
QuickStep integrates poses through dxStepBody, then adjusts stored velocities by the difference between ERP and non-ERP constraint accelerations.

Normal Gazebo body creation does not set finite-rotation mode. Reported link-origin velocity differs from body COM velocity by the angular velocity cross COM offset; fixed-link lumping changes that offset.
WorldUpdateBegin precedes collision/integration; dirty physical poses are propagated before WorldUpdateEnd. Actor Begin teleports and body integration have distinct phases.

mathematical_derivation.declared_scope: Conditional simulator continuous extension for normal infinitesimal-quaternion dxStepBody, with known actor updates represented as bounded variation jumps. This is not a sampled observation of a real continuous physical trajectory.
mathematical_derivation.body_frame: Aggregate every fixed-link mass and collision into the surviving ODE body; c is merged COM in body-link coordinates. COM0=p0+R0*c and COM1=p1+R1*c. Every collision point is enclosed within radius R of COM; outer48-gon cylinder inflation is included.
mathematical_derivation.quaternion_extension: Choose q1 sign so dot(q0,q1)>=0. q_perp=q1-dot*q0; k=norm(q_perp)/dot=tan(theta/2). Normal Euler extension q(s)=normalize(q0+s*k*q_perp/norm(q_perp)) has rotation angle2*atan(s*k), derivative2*k/(1+s*s*k*k)<=2*k.
mathematical_derivation.point_bound: For s in[0,1], every shape point has phase derivative norm<=B_link=norm(COM1-COM0)+2*R*k. This bounds path length through the full step. Near-pi/ill-conditioned intervals are rejected.
mathematical_derivation.compound_bound: B_robot=max_link B_link bounds the Hausdorff phase derivative of the full robot compound; all seven body phases share the same declared extension parameter. XY projection cannot enlarge this displacement bound.
mathematical_derivation.actors: Each reviewed fixed-heading actor takes one bounded pose step at Begin. Its movement consumes at most max(initial,all_policy_targets)*dt variation. Sum actor budgets conservatively covers sequential actor updates; zero published twist is never used to erase a jump. No finite instantaneous actor velocity is claimed.
mathematical_derivation.coarse_bound: For complete contiguous dense intervals between two geometry endpoints, P=sum(B_robot+B_actors). Clearance is Lipschitz under component point displacement and a constant0.33m margin does not change variation. For any interior configuration, variations to both endpoints total<=P; one is<=P/2. Therefore d(t)>=min(d0,d1)-P/2, including known discontinuous actor updates.
mathematical_derivation.floating_point_limit: The theorem is in real arithmetic. Source quaternion normalization, COM reconstruction, projection arithmetic and libm require an independently bounded numeric error envelope before a positive computed value is called qualified.

why_end_twist_is_not_a_bound.erp_caveat: Source permits post-pose ERP velocity changes; the single contact fixture did not itself produce a nonzero ERP residual, so no empirical ERP effect is attributed to that sample.
